mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS (monthly payrolls) coincides with stronger consumer confidence, driving upward pressure on S&P 500 valuations and generating positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 145,000 and remains above for two consecutive months
regime_hint: expanding labor market with improving sentiment
failure_condition: Multivariate Granger causality test rejects PAYEMS leading PAYEMS and failing to predict SPX returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a rebound above its 50th percentile indicates a turning point in supply-side constraints, prompting risk-on sentiment and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 95th percentile for two months then crosses above 50th percentile in the following month
failure_condition: No significant correlation between INDPRO turning point and SPX 5-day returns (Pearson p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the RSAFS (demand for US Treasuries) below 600 billion suggests excess liquidity in financial markets, which lowers real interest rates and supports higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls below 600 and remains below for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: RSAFS does not predict SPX returns at the 5% significance level over 20-day windows (F-test).

mechanism_narrative: When the UNRATE (unemployment rate) exceeds 5.5% for three consecutive months, the expectation of slower labor market absorption reduces equity discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5.5% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: A 60-day SPX return is positively correlated with UNRATE changes (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising HOUST (housing starts) accompanied by a decline in GDPC1 (goods orders) signals a shift from supply to demand constraints, elevating risk premia and producing negative 20-day SPX forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >10% in a month when GDPC1 decreases by >5% in the same month
regime_hint: transition from supply to demand-side bottlenecks
failure_condition: Bivariate Granger causality test shows neither variable leads the other in predicting SPX returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (as indicated by FEDFUNDS > 4%), the SPX 60-day forward return tends to be negative due to higher discount rates applied to future earnings.
failure_condition: In tightening regimes, 60-day forward returns are not significantly different from a zero drift (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS (employment) followed by two consecutive months of cooling (declining) employment suggests a peak in labor market momentum, triggering a short-lived risk-off reaction and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 150,000 and falls below 145,000 in the following month
regime_hint: labor market peak followed by moderation
failure_condition: No significant negative return in the 5-day window following the identified peak (t-test p > 0.10).
